prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: single SQUARE final scene painting for the Mars expedition combination game. Create a dramatic oblique aerial view looking down from just ABOVE and ahead of the rising ascent cabin, about 100 to 200 feet above the ground, with the recognizable small base it built still clearly visible below. This is atmospheric Mars ascent just after launch, not space, not orbit, not a docking picture. One continuous image, no panels or text.
Image 1 gives exact spacecraft identity. The ASCENDING object is ONLY that cream upper cabin with teal round hatch, angular dark front windows and familiar roof-mounted tanks. Give it a plausible small propulsion underside and narrow luminous descending exhaust. Its original long splayed landing legs, feet, lower open truss, ladder and short repaired iron support remain as a recognizable EMPTY LOWER LANDING STAGE on the ground below. Do not lift the whole lander with its legs. No trailing hoses or detached panels. The foreground cabin is the emotional focus, roughly 35 percent of image width, seen in upper three-quarter view with its familiar face visible, occupying upper-right/center without hiding the base. Its exhaust descends toward the empty lower stage, with a modest local dust cloud there, not a dust wall hiding the settlement.
The small improvised base below: image2 supplies ONE compact round cream surface habitat with teal-framed door, small roof dish, ONE original modest solar-panel assembly to the left of its door and little scrubber box on the right. Nearby but safely separated from the launch position is a low red rocky outcrop with a SMALL irregular cave mouth. Within that dark mouth glimpse the snug cream pressure shelter end and its teal door from image3, mostly occluded by protective rock; do not show a giant cavern, enormous open hall or greenhouse outside. A simple low ceramic apron is enough. Beside the outcrop, outdoors, the compact reflective petal-shaped solar furnace from image4 remains recognizable but small. The base is a few practical structures on rough ochre ground, not a city, industrial refinery, grid of pads or repeated arrays. Keep true scale: lander cabin and starter hab similar order of size; furnace smaller. The cave shelter is the longer structure mostly concealed under rock. Clear spatial separation between plume/empty stage and hab/farm.
Camera looks DOWN across these meaningful small landmarks and the warm red ridges around them. Strong sense of rising away from the place the player made habitable, broad Martian landscape continuing beyond. Match references' warm cream/teal retro-industrial equipment, nuanced orange rocks, restrained softly painted scientific illustration and warm upper-left sunlight. No extra spacecraft, people, planets, stars, city, launch tower, giant rocket or orbital horizon. No labels, borders or text.
